title: CAT 2023 Question Paper (Slot 1, PYQ) - Quantitative Aptitude - Geometry
subject: Quantitative Aptitude

questions.q: A quadrilateral $ABCD$ is inscribed in a circle such that $AB : CD = 2 : 1$ and $BC : AD = 5 : 4$. If $AC$ and $BD$ intersect at the point $E$, then $AE : CE$ equals
questions.explain:
In a cyclic quadrilateral, $\Delta ABE \sim \Delta DCE$ (because angles subtended by the same arc are equal: $\angle ABE = \angle DCE$ and $\angle BAE = \angle CDE$). 
From this similarity, the ratio of corresponding sides $AE / DE = BE / CE = AB / DC = 2/1$. Thus, $AE = 2 DE$ and $BE = 2 CE$. 
Also, $\Delta ADE \sim \Delta BCE$, meaning $AD / BC = DE / CE$. Since $BC : AD = 5 : 4$, $AD / BC = 4/5$, so $DE = (4/5) CE$. 
We want the ratio $AE / CE$. Using $AE = 2 DE$, substitute $DE = (4/5) CE$ to get $AE = 2(4/5 CE) = (8/5) CE$. 
Therefore, $AE : CE = 8 : 5$.

questions.q: In a right-angled triangle $\Delta ABC$, the altitude $AB$ is 5 cm, and the base $BC$ is 12 cm . $P$ and $Q$ are two points on $BC$ such that the areas of $\Delta ABP, \Delta ABQ$ and $\Delta ABC$ are in arithmetic progression. If the area of $\Delta ABC$ is 1.5 times the area of $\Delta ABP$, the length of $PQ$, in cm, is
questions.explain:
The total area of $\Delta ABC = \frac{1}{2} \times \text{base} \times \text{height} = \frac{1}{2} \times 12 \times 5 = 30$. 
The area of $\Delta ABC = 1.5 \times \text{Area}(\Delta ABP)$, so $\text{Area}(\Delta ABP) = 30 / 1.5 = 20$. 
The areas $20, \text{Area}(\Delta ABQ), 30$ are in arithmetic progression, which means the middle term $\text{Area}(\Delta ABQ) = (20 + 30) / 2 = 25$. 
Since all three triangles share the same height $AB=5$, their areas are proportional to their bases on line $BC$. 
$\text{Area}(\Delta ABQ) = \frac{1}{2} \times AB \times BQ \implies 25 = 2.5 \times BQ \implies BQ = 10$. 
$\text{Area}(\Delta ABP) = \frac{1}{2} \times AB \times BP \implies 20 = 2.5 \times BP \implies BP = 8$. 
The points lie on the same line segment $BC$, so $PQ = BQ - BP = 10 - 8 = 2$ cm.
